items.headline: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
items.blurb: Six people were killed in a random shooting in the city's main square, and three bodies were later found at the home of the attacker.
items.text: At least six people were killed and more than a dozen others injured when a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland. Three bodies were found at his home when it was searched by police. Here is everything we know so far. The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city which is popular with tourists. Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car". Footage from the scene shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard. A passing tram was shot at during the apparently random attack, shattering windows but no passengers were injured. Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said. items.text: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk describes a deadly shooting in Krakow that killed six people and wounded 15 as an act of ‘terrorism’. Three more bodies, believed to be members of the suspect’s family, were found at his home.

items.headline: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
items.blurb: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.
items.text: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history. The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes. Prosecutors said Paul Mackenzie and his Good News International church ran ​a Christian doomsday sect whose members were ordered to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended. His accomplices threatened and beat victims to ensure they followed his orders. The emaciated bodies were found scattered in shallow graves and dumped in latrines. Some had been buried alive. items.headline: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
items.blurb: Neither PM Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor that of his rival secured a majority in last week's election.
items.text: Israel's president says he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government. Isaac Herzog has been holding talks with political parties after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a majority in Israel's parliament, known as the Knesset, following last week's election. Eisenkot will now have 28 days to try to form a new administration, with a potential 14-day extension. "Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy," the former military chief wrote on X. No political party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, meaning all governments have been coalitions. Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48. Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters. That positions them as potential kingmakers. items.headline: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted
items.blurb: Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80%…
items.text: Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted. Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party . The former liberation movement is projected to lose its status as the biggest party in the two most populous provinces, Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal, as parties began coalition negotiations behind closed doors. The final results are expected to be announced on Sunday. The ANC was on 31.8% of the vote nationally, almost 14 percentage points below its 2021 local election result. items.headline: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
items.blurb: Weeks of coalition talks could follow after preliminary results pointed to a highly divided national parliament.
items.text: There was no clear winner following New Zealand's election on Saturday, as the leaders of its two major parties preparing for negotiations to form a coalition government. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right National Party won 42 seats but was 19 short of the simple majority needed to form a government, despite being the largest party, preliminary results show. Combined with their coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First, they would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc if a deal could be reached. But opposition leader Chris Hipkins, whose Labour Party won 36 seats, showed no signs of conceding, saying the "shape of the next government" will remain uncertain "for a while". The tight result followed a campaign shaped by the cost of living and unemployment. Projections show the National Party on 42 seats and Labour on 36. The Greens are on 16, with ACT on 13, New Zealand First on 12, the Opportunity Party on 7 and Te Pāti Māori, which represents Māori interests, on 5. items.headline: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3–0 to draw level with La Liga leaders Barcelona
items.blurb: Valverde and Guler's first-half goals put Madrid in the driving seat, and Mbappe added a third in the second half.
items.text: Kylian Mbappe scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3–0 win at 10-man Valencia. Reigning champions Barca visit Atletico Madrid , third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack. Jose Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla Stadium on Saturday, securing an eighth win in a row across all competitions. Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first-half goals put Madrid in the driving seat, and Mbappe added a third in the second half. Los Blancos were without winger Vinicius Junior, who was serving the final game of a four-match ban. Madrid have thrived in his absence, putting heavy pressure on Barca, whom they beat in the Camp Nou Clasico on October 25. In the ninth minute, the match stopped for players and fans to pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who tragically died on Tuesday. items.blurb: Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed.
items.text: Patient is ⁠in ​stable condition and will be transferred to a specialist ‘high consequence’ infectious disease unit A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed. “A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola ,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday. “The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.” The patient, whose identity is unknown, is in a stable condition and is expected to arrive in the UK on Wednesday or Thursday before being transferred in a specialist ambulance to a “high consequence” infectious disease unit, according to an official document seen by Reuters. A humanitarian organisation sent the worker to DR Congo to help in the response to the outbreak, which is the second largest on record. items.headline: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
items.blurb: Donald Trump has repeatedly raised the prospect of renewing strikes against Iran's nuclear facilities.
items.text: The US has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear programme. The State Department's Rewards for Justice is also offering to potentially relocate the person who provides such details. President Donald Trump claimed last year that Iran's nuclear facilities had been "completely and totally obliterated " following a bombing campaign by the US and Israel. Iran insists its nuclear programme is peaceful and that it has no intention of developing a nuclear weapon. Meanwhile, the US military says it is setting up a task force to enhance Washington's efforts to restrict Iran's movement of weapons and sanctioned material across its borders. The US military's Central Command (Centcom) said Task Force Iron Gate would operate from Tampa, Florida, and would work with other US government agencies. As well as the movement of weapons, it will also focus on dual-use and illegal revenue streams. Centcom estimates that its naval blockade of Iran's ports has prevented the country from exporting more than $25bn in crude oil. items.headline: A bridge between past and present
items.blurb: A German publication ranked Bihar Museum among the best in the world. Mayank Kumar visits to understand what went into the making of the museum and what visitors think of its contribution to the development of Indian civilization
items.text: Designed by Japan’s Maki & Associates in partnership with Pune-based _Opolis Architects, Bihar Museum combines traditional storytelling with the contemporary principles of New Museology. | Photo Credit: Mayank Kumar On November 3, Soumya Pathak, 23, a final-year medical student studying at a medical college in Ambala, Haryana, is exploring exhibits showcasing relics from prehistoric times at the Bihar Museum in Patna. Pathak belongs to Muzaffarpur in Bihar, and is looking at some coins from the Mauryan (321–185 B.C.E) and Gupta ages (early 4th to mid-6th Century C.E.). She passes through interactive galleries which highlight Bihar’s pivotal role in shaping two major world religions: Jainism and Buddhism. “I have been thinking of coming here for a long time, but after reading on social media that the museum is ranked the best in Asia, I decided to spend a day here,” she says. Pathak is enroute to Muzaffarpur for the Deepavali holidays and came to the museum directly from Patna’s Jay Prakash Narayan airport, about four kilometres away. items.headline: Singapore-based executive shot dead at Faridabad home after disputes over parking, pet dog
items.blurb: Police say the suspect fired multiple rounds and was arrested the next day. Relatives say the families had argued over a dog and parking-related issues.
items.text: A 43-year-old software company executive who lived in Singapore was allegedly shot dead by a neighbour at his Faridabad family residence late on Friday, with the assailant firing 15–19 rounds that left the victim dead at the spot. The victim was identified as Paramjith Dhankhar, 43, who was employed by Vietnam-based FPT Software Company Limited at its Singapore office and was visiting his family for Diwali . He was previously a senior executive at Indian tech firm Tech Mahindra . The suspect was identified as 42-year-old Mohan Sharma, a contractor and scrap-processing businessman. He was arrested from Ballabgarh on Saturday and his licensed handgun, with 59 live cartridges kept inside the bag used for storing the weapon, and two magazines—one of which was partially loaded—were recovered, police said. The two men lived on different floors of four-storey building in Faridabad’s Sector 21C. items.headline: Ahead of Deepavali, Chhath festivals, migrants reach Bihar in hordes covering thousands of kilometers
items.blurb: Four young men on Saturday (November 7, 2026), from Bengaluru, travelled about 2,200 km riding on an old auto-rickshaw to reach Areraj town, in East Champaran
items.text: Ahead of Deepavali and the four-day Chhath festival, migrants are visiting different places of Bihar in hordes. With the flight fares skyrocketing and train ticket charts shown full, migrants are reaching their destination by buses and even riding on old auto-rickshaws covering thousands of kilometres. Four young men on Saturday (November 7, 2026), from Bengaluru, travelled about 2,200 km riding on an old auto-rickshaw to reach Areraj town, near Someshwarnath Dham temple in Motihari of East Champaran district in Bihar. Reaching their destination in three days, they told local media persons that it was their “desire to celebrate Deepavali and Chhath festival along with family members” and the air ticket fares had gone beyond their capacity. With train ticket charts shown chock-a-bloc they, eventually, decided to travel to their village in Areraj by riding on the old auto-rickshaw, which one of them runs in Bengaluru for a living. items.headline: PM Modi extends Diwali wishes, to celebrate festival with jawans today
items.blurb: PM Modi extended Diwali greetings to people across the country on Sunday. He will be celebrating the festival with the jawans.
items.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday extended Diwali greetings to the people across the country, wishing everyone on the occasion of the festival of lights. On Saturday, the Prime Minister had conveyed his festive greetings, wishing the people happiness, peace and prosperity. He reiterated his tradition of celebrating Diwali with jawans, continuing his annual gesture of spending the festival with armed forces personnel. “Diwali wishes to everyone! Heartfelt Diwali wishes to my family members across the country,” PM Modi said in his latest post on X. On Saturday, PM Modi had extended Diwali greetings to the nation through a video message, highlighting the festival as a symbol of light’s triumph over darkness and expressing hope for happiness, peace and prosperity for all citizens. In a 50-second video message shared on social media platforms including X, Modi appeared in traditional attire with a tilak and addressed people directly, extending his greetings on the festival. He said the country was glowing with lights on the occasion of Deepavali. “This festival of light is a reflection of our resolve against darkness,” he remarked.

items.headline: RJD MP Sanjay Yadav writes to President, seeks action against DU Professor Sangeet Ragi
items.blurb: Mr. Yadav said that Mr. Ragi used the abusive language against Yadav community on behest of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
items.text: Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader and Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Yadav wrote a letter to President Draupadi Murmu, requesting her to order strict action against Delhi University Professor Sangeet Ragi for allegedly insulting the Yadav community. Mr. Yadav said that he used the abusive language on behest of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He mentioned that action is necessary so that it serves as an exemplary punishment, ensuring that in a diverse country like India, no one dares to insult any society, class or community in the name of freedom of expression, and thus hurting unity and integrity of the nation. The three-page letter dated November 6, 2026, was shared with media on Saturday (November 7, 2026). “I am writing to you in my capacity as a Member of Parliament (Rajyasabha) to express my serious concern regarding the alleged caste-based derogatory remarks made by Professor Sangeet Ragi of the University of Delhi against India’s largest community (Yadav/Ahir) during a televised public debate,” Mr. Yadav stated. items.headline: Delhi breathes worst air on Diwali eve in 10 years
items.blurb: Weak winds are forecast to trap pollution, with forecasts suggesting air quality could reach the severe category by Monday.
items.text: Delhi wakes up to Diwali on Sunday after its most polluted festival eve in a decade, with a perfect storm gathering over the night to come. Farm fires in Punjab and Haryana climbed to their highest this season on Saturday — and the Isro satellite’s count rose for a 10th straight day, the ground wind fell calm after sunset, and within two hours of the first evening window for firecrackers opening at 8pm, the city’s air was 30% dirtier than a night earlier. All of that came before the festival night itself, when most of the city’s firecrackers are burst, and light winds are forecast for Sunday. The 4pm air quality index ( AQI ) on Saturday was 369, “very poor” on the Central Pollution Control Board ’s (CPCB) 0–500 scale and the highest for the day before Diwali since 2016, when it was 404. The index, an average of the past 24 hours, has climbed from 261 on November 1. items.headline: High fares, longer journeys, delays make special trains less attractive to passengers: Officials
items.blurb: Railway Ministry claims to operate special trains during the festive rush, yet regular train demand exceeds their capacity. Special trains often have higher fares and longer travel durations compared to regular trains, which leads to disappointment among travelers.
items.text: Railway Ministry claims to operate special trains during the festive rush, yet regular train demand exceeds their capacity. Special trains often have higher fares and longer travel durations compared to regular trains, which leads to disappointment among travelers. Many passengers are willing to book waiting-list tickets for regular trains due to their reliability and punctuality. Railway officials suggest lowering special train fares to attract more passengers amidst ongoing challenges.

items.headline: Kirloskar Industries Q2 profit rises 5% to ₹105 crore, income up 17%
items.blurb: Kirloskar Industries Ltd (KIL) has reported a 5 per cent rise in consolidated profit after tax to Rs 105 crore in the quarter ended September 2026. The company had posted a consolidated PAT (profit after tax) of Rs 100.1 crore in the year-ago period.
items.text: Kirloskar Industries Ltd (KIL) has reported a 5 per cent rise in consolidated profit after tax to ₹105 crore in the quarter ended September 2026. The company had posted a consolidated PAT (profit after tax) of ₹100.1 crore in the year-ago period. Consolidated income of the company during the second quarter rose to ₹2,097.7 crore from ₹1,790.1 crore in the year-ago period, KIL said in a statement. "Our material subsidiary, Kirloskar Ferrous Industries Limited, continued to deliver a resilient performance during the year, supported by operational stability, capacity optimisation and strong demand for its products across the sectors. On the real estate front, our wholly-owned subsidiary, Avante Spaces Limited (ASL), is progressing well. Our landmark Kothrud project is going well and moving forward on track, reinforcing our vision of creating premium, future-ready spaces that maximise value for our stakeholders," George Verghese, Managing Director, KIL, said. Kirloskar Industries Limited is the core investment company of the Kirloskar Group, one of India's oldest and most diversified business conglomerates with a legacy spanning over 135 years. items.headline: NIT Raipur, AKSI Aerospace join hands, set-up Centre Of Excellence: What will the new partnership focus on?
items.blurb: NIT Raipur and AKSI Aerospace Group plan to establish a Centre of Excellence for aerospace and autonomous technologies, alongside a manufacturing facility. The partnership will connect research with industrial production, provide hands-on training, and support India’s indigenous drone capabilities.
items.text: The National Institute of Technology (NIT), Raipur, has partnered with AKSI Aerospace Group to establish a Centre of Excellence (CoE) focused on aerospace and autonomous technologies, with plans to connect academic research with industrial applications and strengthen India's indigenous drone technology capabilities. The proposed centre will work on areas such as droneplatforms, flight control systems, propulsion, batteries, advanced materials and autonomous technologies. It aims to give students and researchers hands-on exposure to engineering challenges, including prototyping, manufacturing, system integration and testing, according to a press release. The initiative is intended to take research beyond academic settings by helping convert ideas into practical prototypes and industry-oriented solutions. It will also facilitate collaborative research, student projects, technical training and industry mentorship, with the broader aim of developing talent equipped to work in the aerospace and unmanned aerial vehicle ( UAV ) sectors. Alongside the Centre of Excellence, AKSI Aerospace plans to establish a manufacturing facility in Raipur. items.headline: Labubu hype seemed unstoppable, now the fluffy monster mania is dying
items.blurb: Parent company Pop Mart's revenue has fallen as appetite for the quirky collectible monsters wanes.
items.text: Collectors young and old energetically snapped up "blind boxes" - sealed, mystery packages containing the quirky monsters - often paying $15 (£11) or more. Those unable to get the characters they wanted were often prepared to pay much more on the resale market. The hype around the creatures convinced a mega-fan from North Carolina, who goes by the name Ensito, to leave his tech job in 2024 to create Labubu content full-time, travelling as far as Italy and Spain to seek out the latest releases. Ensito has spent more than $50,000 (£37,000) to build his collection of more than 400 Labubus, a figure he tells the BBC he's "embarrassed to say". He even had a row of custom Labubu-like jagged teeth made by a dentist to wear at events. But in recent months, Ensito's once-viral posts about the furry monsters have struggled. "Those videos used to be able to hit 10,000 really quickly but I'm struggling to do that now." Ensito's focus has shifted to other trends like Hello Kitty and squishies. items.blurb: Peak XV Partners, Y Combinator and Goldman Sachs have sold a combined 2 per cent stake in Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of Groww, for Rs 2,457 crore, according to bulk deal data on the BSE and NSE.
items.text: Peak XV Partners, Y Combinator and Goldman Sachs have sold a combined 2 per cent stake in Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of Groww, for ₹2,457 crore, according to bulk deal data on the BSE and NSE. The three investors offloaded more than 11.52 crore shares, representing a combined 1.84 per cent stake in Groww on Friday, as per the data. US-based Peak XV Partners, through its arm Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1, sold more than 6 crore shares, and Goldman Sachs divested 4,380 shares of Groww on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). In addition, Y Combinator, through its arm YC Holdings II, LLC, disposed of 5.50 crore shares on the BSE. The shares were disposed of in the price range of ₹211.09–215.20 apiece, taking the combined deal value to ₹2,456.87 crore. Details of other buyers of Groww's shares could not be identified on the exchanges. items.blurb: The acquisition was expected to strengthen SoftBank’s revenue and profitability as the Japanese investment firm continues to expand its AI portfolio and awaits a potential financial boost from OpenAI’s anticipated public listing
items.text: China has blocked Japanese investment conglomerate SoftBank Group’s proposed $5.4 billion acquisition of the robotics business of Swiss-Swedish engineering giant ABB , dealing a significant setback to founder Masayoshi Son’s ambitions to expand into physical artificial intelligence (AI). According to a report by The Japan Times , ABB confirmed that a Chinese government agency had prohibited the transaction. The decision highlights Beijing’s growing scrutiny of foreign investments in strategically important technology businesses amid intensifying global competition in artificial intelligence and robotics. The acquisition was expected to strengthen SoftBank’s revenue and profitability as the Japanese investment firm continues to expand its AI portfolio and awaits a potential financial boost from OpenAI’s anticipated public listing. SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son had identified the proposed acquisition as an important part of his strategy to establish a stronger position in the emerging physical AI industry. items.headline: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage

The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep.
items.text: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents. This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem. Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient.
